clue.text: Artist having great worry about trophy requiring line engraved

indicators.note: about tells us the worry goes round the other pieces

parts.note: stress is great worry or strain

indicators.note: engraved means the line is cut into the trophy, sitting inside it

parts.note: a cup is a trophy won in sport

explanation.surface: A painter fretting over a cup that needs a line cut into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engraved' makes CULP, which 'about' surrounds. 'Artist' tempts a painter, but this one works in stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A female sculptor is a kind of artist, so the general term covers her.

clue.text: Wise attitude missing in early historical period

indicators.note: missing tells us the attitude is taken out of the period

parts.note: the Stone Age is the earliest period of human prehistory
tone can mean attitude, as in the tone of a letter

explanation.surface: A wise outlook absent from an early stage of history.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone sage has deep wisdom and sound judgement.

clue.text: Old thought, to avoid getting married

indicators.note: to avoid tells us the married letter is left out of the word for thought

parts.note: mused means thought or pondered
M is the abbreviation for married, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: An old idea, held by someone keen not to get wed.
explanation.definitionFit: Secondhand goods are called old or worn, as in a pre-owned car.

clue.text: Mourn with passion, distraught — something many can't get over

indicators.note: distraught means wildly upset, so the letters of these two words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Grieving passionately, distraught over a loss many never get past.
explanation.walkthrough: PONS ASINORUM, Latin for 'bridge of asses', is Euclid's theorem on isosceles triangles, a test weak pupils could not cross.
explanation.definitionFit: The bridge of asses is a proverbial hurdle that slow learners fail to cross, a witty twist on getting over grief.

clue.text: Pay increase? Beams, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for beams is spoken, and a word sounding the same is entered

parts.note: beams of light are rays

explanation.surface: A worker smiling at a salary rise, beaming.
explanation.definitionFit: A raise is the American and informal British word for an increase in salary.

clue.text: Bag about to wrap around one support, showing disrespect

parts.note: a sac is a bag-like pouch in a body

indicators.note: to wrap around means the word for about encloses the other pieces

parts.note: re means about or concerning
I is the Roman numeral one
a leg supports a table or chair

explanation.surface: Someone wrapping a bag round a prop, in a way that shows contempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to wrap around' gives RILEGE; 'showing' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacrilege is gross disrespect toward something held sacred.

clue.text: Senior officer keeping it back for hearing?

indicators.note: back says the whole assembly is read in the opposite direction
keeping means the officer holds the word it inside

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer

explanation.surface: A commanding officer holding something back for a hearing, like a tribunal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' gives COIT, which 'back' turns round. 'Hearing' suggests a tribunal but means the sense of hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Otic is the medical adjective relating to the ear and so to the sense of sound.

clue.text: Banter I see interrupting guy in charge — that's not entirely funny

indicators.note: interrupting means these pieces break into the middle of the guy in charge

parts.note: Tom is any man's name, so stands for a guy
to rag is to tease or banter
the letter C is pronounced like the word see

explanation.surface: Someone teasing a boss and getting a mixed reception.
explanation.walkthrough: RAGIC goes inside TOMIC after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tragicomic mixes sadness with humour, so it is only partly comic.

clue.text: Copper assesses, say, head of gang: "One's not entirely bad"

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
rates means assesses or values
eg, for example, is what 'say' means

indicators.note: head of picks out the first letter of the word gang

explanation.surface: A policeman sizing up a gang leader and finding him not wholly bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the chemical element. The phrase comes from a Punch cartoon where a curate calls his bad egg 'good in parts'.
explanation.definitionFit: A curate's egg is a thing partly good and partly poor, mixed in quality.

clue.text: Inexperienced fielder's beginning to move slowly, getting the bird

parts.note: green means inexperienced or new to something

indicators.note: beginning picks out the first letter of fielder's

parts.note: to inch is to move slowly, little by little

explanation.surface: A novice cricket fielder plodding along and being jeered for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting the bird' suggests being booed off, but the bird is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The greenfinch is a common olive-green finch of Europe.

clue.text: Poor performance with the bat? I put in standard performance

indicators.note: put in tells us I goes inside the word for standard performance

parts.note: par is the standard expected score, as in golf

explanation.surface: A batsman admitting a dismal innings after an ordinary display.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a pair is being out for no runs in both innings of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Two ducks in one match, called a pair, are the worst batting showing possible.

clue.text: Unexpectedly erratic about moving onstage

indicators.note: about puts the word for erratic round the reordered letters

parts.note: stray can mean erratic or wandering, as in a stray bullet

indicators.note: moving tells us the letters of onstage are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: An actor wandering erratically about the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges the stage word into ANGETOS, which 'about' places inside the erratic word after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a sentence adverb meaning surprisingly or oddly enough.

clue.text: Kendal sadly overlooking new firm behind one tourist area

indicators.note: behind places the word for firm after one
sadly works as an anagram signal: the letters of the town are badly arranged
overlooking means leaving out, so the new letter is dropped

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
strict means firm, as in a firm parent

explanation.surface: Kendal, sadly passed over when a new business sets up behind a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooking' drops N from KENDAL; 'sadly' turns KEDAL into LAKED. Kendal is a town in Cumbria, on the edge of the Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lake District in north-west England is a national park visited by millions.

clue.text: Scottish community willing tho' disturbed

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters of these words are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A Scottish town keen enough, though troubled.
explanation.definitionFit: Linlithgow is a town in West Lothian, birthplace of Mary, Queen of Scots.

clue.text: Hanger-on to get hard sugary item

parts.note: a sponge is someone who lives off others
to cake is to harden into a crust, as mud does

explanation.surface: A freeloader hardening up a sweet treat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponge cake is a light sweet cake made with sugar, eggs and flour.

clue.text: Involve mischief-maker with story about jazz fan

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child or sprite

indicators.note: about says the story goes round the jazz fan

parts.note: a lie is a story in the sense of a fib
cat is jazz slang for a fan or player

explanation.surface: Dragging a prankster into a tale about a jazz enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: To implicate someone is to show them to be involved in a crime or affair.

clue.text: Tumbling, I fail, after missing right branch

indicators.note: tumbling suggests a fall, so the letters are tossed about
missing tells us the right letter is absent from after

explanation.surface: A climber falling and missing the correct bough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' leaves AFTE, and 'Tumbling' shuffles that with the first two words.
explanation.definitionFit: An affiliate is a branch or associated organisation linked to a larger body.

clue.text: Declares Bible arguments should have Rector dismissed

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible

indicators.note: dismissed means the rector is sent out of the word for arguments

parts.note: rows are noisy quarrels

explanation.surface: Someone stating that scriptural disputes should end with the vicar removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To avow is to declare or assert openly.

clue.text: Language traditional in Government, to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark on old-fashioned jargon heard in Whitehall.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingo is informal for a language, especially a foreign or specialist one.

clue.text: Young bird escaped to rear of waving heather

parts.note: fled means escaped

indicators.note: rear of picks out the last letter of waving

parts.note: ling is another name for heather

explanation.surface: A chick flies off to the back of the swaying heather.
explanation.definitionFit: A fledgling is a young bird that has just grown the feathers to fly.

clue.text: What Field-Marshal's biography should deliver?

parts.note: Field-Marshal Montgomery was known as Monty, so a complete life of him tells all about the man

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means everything that is required, the complete works.

clue.text: Source of tension apparent in nothing currently being drawn

parts.note: O is the zero symbol, so nothing

indicators.note: apparent in says the letter shows up inside the word for currently

parts.note: now means currently

indicators.note: source of picks out the first letter of tension

explanation.surface: Signs of strain showing as nothing is being sketched at present.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle on tow is being pulled behind another one.

clue.text: Paints switching ends in storage facility

indicators.note: switching, with ends, says the first and last letters of the word for paints trade places
ends names the outer letters of the word for paints as the ones that move

parts.note: oils are oil paints

explanation.surface: A painter swapping colours around in a storeroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switching ends' swaps the O and S at either end of OILS: one end letter moves to the back, the other to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A silo is a tower or pit for storing grain or silage.

clue.text: Given guidance about new grant

indicators.note: about places the word for guided round the new letter

parts.note: led means guided

explanation.surface: Advice was offered regarding a fresh funding award.
explanation.definitionFit: To lend can mean to grant or give, as in lend support.

clue.text: Claim runs in game, after reverse

indicators.note: in puts the runs letter inside the reversed game
after reverse says the word for game is read backwards

parts.note: a bag is the game shot in a day's hunting
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricketer claiming runs in a match after a setback.
explanation.definitionFit: To grab something can mean to claim or seize it, as in grab a seat.

clue.text: Attention of old solvers absorbing quiet lunar phenomenon

parts.note: to give an ear is to pay attention

indicators.note: absorbing means the old word for yours takes in the call for quiet

parts.note: thine is the archaic form of yours, belonging to you solvers
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: Puzzlers of yesteryear quietly taking in a moon effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthshine is sunlight reflected from Earth that faintly lights the dark part of the Moon.

clue.text: Question about English dairy product

indicators.note: about says the question word goes round the letter for English

parts.note: why is a question word

explanation.surface: A query about an English dairy item.
explanation.definitionFit: Whey is the watery liquid left after milk curdles in cheesemaking.

clue.text: Welsh town to gamble with opening of some unknown school

parts.note: to bet is to gamble

indicators.note: opening of picks out the first letter of some

parts.note: Y is a mathematical unknown
a coed is a mixed school

explanation.surface: Someone in a Welsh town betting on a new school.
explanation.definitionFit: Betws-y-Coed is a village in Snowdonia, North Wales, popular with visitors.
